FORMAL IMPLEMENTATION / REPRODUCIBILITY REVIEW — BLOCK

Reviewer: codex-mockup-implementation-review
Candidate: cand-3CM1JDY29SG3WPSV74GVS08WNF
Commit: dda53463a1556f1b18bfd8a24c937d439fc89dfc
Tree: 7fd21caf66b562c48c635ba38844ad00ffd7303b
Direct parent and base: 003f12b21e1b9793fea479e104c2e2eff3e55fe5

Identity and scope

I reviewed a detached disposable clone of the exact candidate. Git independently confirms the stated commit, tree, direct parent, and a diff confined to mockups/mockup-v2-design-brief.md and mockups/v2. git diff --check is clean. No authoritative checkout, candidate byte, index, branch, authorization, landing, or remote was changed.

Repaired gates that pass

I3b passes independently. node mockups/v2/verify-manifest.cjs verified 25 artifact sources, 29 artifact outputs, 25 reproducible sources, and 14 reproducible outputs. Exact digests are artifact 3dd04832dbbe9a3501f5af3048378a62d9809362aa10e04164ac550835dca9e8 and reproducible d3a378c3444d3e6d435ba6b1f9e4663499be52a895bb03fb9b0f13d5f84a5530. The actual directory inventories are exactly 25 and 29 with no missing or extra paths.

I independently mutated the exact serialized manifest in memory and reauthenticated each changed reproducible target. All three prior counterexamples are killed:
- false reproducible.sourceSetDigest: reproducible projection does not match the verified artifact;
- false reproducible.sources[0].sha256: reproducible sources/Compact.dc.html digest drift;
- false reproducible.outputs[0].sha256: reproducible outputs/compact.html digest drift.
Reauthenticated artifact-only source and output hash mutations also fail against actual bytes. manifest-digest.cjs:60-80 now defines one canonical reproducibleProjection; lines 126-132 verify both byte sets and require canonical equality to that projection. This repairs I3b.

The prior outer-ancestor I2b mutation also passes its requested retest. Two unpiped exact runs of node mockups/v2/export.cjs each exited zero with 13 plates under Chromium 140.0.7339.186 and reproduced both signed digests above. The built-in one-pixel overflow-hidden wrapper around compact-codex is killed with observation-clipped-by-ancestor. The successful exact runs also re-executed strict directive, visible-root, fixture, feature-ledger, claim-span, frozen-resource, plate, and manifest mutation courts. The candidate source/output bytes reproduced; only diagnostics.generatorContext.preCommitSourceHead changed from the checked-in pre-commit value 343aa625 to the exact reviewed SHA. That field is explicitly unsigned, while both signed digests stayed identical.

Browser ownership audits before and after all exact and adversarial probes reported no automated top-level browser process. The exact fixture court passed. I did not substitute these checks for the separately registered exact sbt evidence.

Blocking residual in I2b: self-clipping exact evidence is omitted from the clipping chain

PROOF-BOUNDARY.md:33-37 claims exact evidence typography and reachability have killing mutations and that no content-bearing exact-evidence region is silently clipped by its scroll viewport or an outer clipping ancestor. The prior acceptance note also required inspection of a clipping evidence element itself.

The implementation does not meet that boundary. export.cjs:377-385 defines clippingAncestors(item) but begins at item.parentElement. Lines 388-404 therefore inspect only ancestors for scrollWidth/clientWidth overflow. Lines 413-445 compare the item bounding rectangle with cumulative ancestor bounds, but never compare the item own scroll extent with its client extent. A self-clipped one-pixel element has a one-pixel bounding rectangle that is fully inside every ancestor, so it is certified.

Independent exact-court counterexample

I loaded the exact candidate export.cjs bytes in a VM solely to expose its unchanged plateCourt function, opened the exact frozen compact.html, and changed the first s01 observation element in the browser DOM to:

display:inline-block; width:1px; overflow:hidden; white-space:nowrap

The browser measured clientWidth=1, scrollWidth=279, rectWidth=1, overflowX=hidden for the text At first light two boats were. Thus 278 pixels of exact evidence were silently clipped by the evidence element itself.

The exact candidate plateCourt nevertheless returned no error with:
- all s01-s10 observation byte checks present;
- exact typography passing;
- clippedEvidence=[];
- reachability=[compact-codex];
- offenders=[].

This is a capacity-to-fail defect in the same evidence-clipping law, not a visual preference. The repaired outer-ancestor mutation distinguishes one ancestor case but does not sweep the clipping shape to the marked element itself.

Minimum successor acceptance

1. Replace the parent-only traversal with an element-plus-ancestor clipping chain, or separately inspect every data-observation-ref own overflow axes and scroll extent before ancestor traversal.
2. For a non-scroll evidence element, fail when an overflow hidden/clip axis has scrollWidth greater than clientWidth or scrollHeight greater than clientHeight beyond tolerance. Retain the cumulative ancestor and scrollIntoView checks.
3. Add an independent mutation on an evidence element itself: set one exact span to one-pixel width, overflow hidden, and nowrap; assert the court fails for that same observation ref. Restore the style before the screenshot.
4. Keep the existing outer one-pixel ancestor mutation and the now-correct I3b mutations. Both self and ancestor cases must fail for distinct, inspectable reasons.

No additional artifact or reproducibility blocker was found in this pass. Formal disposition remains BLOCK solely because the executable proof boundary still certifies demonstrably clipped exact evidence. This review does not authorize or land the candidate.
